title: A hot plate with two coils
body: An electric hot plate works on a 220 V supply. Inside it are two identical heating coils, P and Q, each of resistance 55 ohm. A selector switch lets the user operate the hot plate in three ways: only one coil connected across the supply, both coils joined in series across the supply, or both coils joined in parallel across the supply. The supply voltage stays at 220 V in every setting, and the resistance of each coil may be taken as constant. The manufacturer labels the settings 'Low', 'Medium' and 'High' according to the rate at which heat is produced.

title: A family's electricity use
body: A family records how they use three appliances every day for 30 days. A 2000 W water heater (geyser) runs for 30 minutes each morning. A 250 W television runs for 4 hours each evening. Five LED lamps, each rated 12 W, stay on for 6 hours each night. All appliances work at their rated power on a 220 V supply. The electricity company charges Rs 6.00 for every kilowatt hour (one 'unit') of energy used.
